title: The Long Way Is Shorter
scene: Willis dead-ends into a berm somebody pushed up and never came back for. The insulin has forty minutes of cold left and the reroute is behind you. Residential, both sides, driveways every fifty feet. Gracie is up on the dash. Reverse lights are the brightest thing this car makes, and every second of backing is a second the mirrors are doing the work your eyes should be doing.
decision: You have to reverse direction. How?

options.text: Drive the block — right at the corner, right again, back onto Willis facing out
options.result: Four right turns, no reverse gear, no white lights. You come back onto Willis pointed at the arterial with the berm behind you. It cost ninety seconds and it cost nothing else.

options.text: U-turn right here — the street is empty and it takes four seconds
options.result: You swing it and the nose comes around across a double yellow you did not look down at. It works. It also would not have, three feet later, where the road narrows and the drainage grate sits. The yellow was there the whole time.

options.text: Back into the nearest driveway and come out the other way
options.result: It works, and it takes you twenty feet of reverse with the white lights on and the mirrors doing all of it. Not wrong. Just more backing than the corner would have cost you, on a street where backing is the expensive thing.

options.text: Three-point turn in the lane — forward, reverse, forward
options.result: You end up crosswise in a residential lane with the nose in one gutter and the tail in the other, reverse lights on, going nowhere for a beat and a half. Anything coming around the corner arrives at a car that is a wall.

debrief: The safest way to turn a vehicle around is to drive around the block. Less backing is always better — backing is slower, blinder, and it is when you are least able to leave. Save the two-point and the three-point for when there is no block to drive.

source.teaching_target: Driving around the block is the safest turnaround; minimize backing. U-turns are prohibited across a double yellow line.

image_brief.subject: orthographic overhead of a residential block, the Pink Menace stopped short of a dirt berm blocking the street end
image_brief.foreground: clean overhead lane geometry, painted double yellow centerline running the length of Willis, driveways spaced along both sides
image_brief.midground: the four-right-turn loop around the block readable as open roadway; the berm as a hard stop across the far end
image_brief.background: wet residential rooftops and bare trees, flat gray overcast, no shadows
image_brief.read: the double yellow centerline is unbroken beneath the car, and a complete open loop exists around the block — both facts legible at a glance

title: Two Hundred Feet of Willis
scene: The corner is gone too — a transformer came down across it in the night and the wires are still on the pole. No block to drive. Four driveways in reach: one across the street, one thirty feet up on your side against a blind hedge, one on your side with clean sight down Willis, one behind you past the crest. Insulin, thirty minutes.
decision: No block. You are backing into a driveway. Which one?

options.text: Your side, the one with clear sight down Willis — signal, check behind, back in
options.result: You pull just past it, blinker on, nothing behind you, and reverse in with two hundred feet of empty road in the mirror the whole time. Shift to drive, check both ways, and roll out pointed the right direction.

options.text: The one across the street — it is the widest and the apron is flat
options.result: Backing into it means dragging the car across the oncoming lane and sitting in it, sideways, blind to the crest. The apron is flat and it does not matter. You are a gate across the only road.

options.text: The near one at thirty feet — closest, least time exposed
options.result: The hedge eats Willis at about eighty feet. You are in reverse with a sightline shorter than your stopping distance, and the first thing you would know about anything coming is the sound of it.

options.text: Past the crest behind you — the driveway there is long and straight
options.result: You reverse up and over the crest to reach it, which means backing blind over the one piece of road you cannot see the far side of. The driveway is fine. Everything before the driveway is not.

debrief: A two-point turn backs into a driveway on the same side of the street as your car, at a spot with at least two hundred feet of visible oncoming road. Pull just past it, signal, confirm nothing is behind you, then reverse. Shift to drive and check both directions before you pull out.

source.teaching_target: Two-point turn: same-side driveway, 200 feet of visible oncoming traffic, signal, confirm clear behind, back in, then check both directions before pulling out.

image_brief.subject: the mirror on the left side of the vehicle, seen from inside the cabin, filled with a long clear stretch of empty wet residential street behind the car
image_brief.foreground: the mirror housing and a slice of riveted steel door plating, sharply in focus
image_brief.midground: a paved driveway apron entering frame at the mirror's edge on the same side as the car
image_brief.background: Willis running straight and empty to a distant vanishing point, bare maples, flat gray overcast
image_brief.read: the road behind is visibly long, straight and unobstructed, and the driveway sits on the same side as the mirror
